Rachel / Monica — summary of technical constraints and what we can provide for Veridian:

- Regions: For Private deployments the supported US regions for the pilot are us-west-2 (Oregon) and us-east-1 (N. Virginia). We will pin the pilot to a single region per deployment; cross-region replication is available only if explicitly enabled and requires customer sign-off (not enabled by default).

- VPC/private control plane: We support two deployment modes for Private: (1) Private control plane (managed by Redwood but accessible only over private connectivity to the customer's VPC) and (2) Customer-run control plane (entirely inside customer VPC / on-prem). For Veridian's pilot we recommend mode (1) with an AWS PrivateLink endpoint into your VPC. This keeps the runtime inside your chosen region while allowing Redwood to manage HA and autoscaling.

- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS for data-at-rest encryption on Private deployments. Integration types:
  * Bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) where Veridian supplies key ARN and Redwood configures the cluster to use it.
  * Customer HSM gateway (partners) available on request — requires additional onboarding.

- Audit logs: Request/response logs and infra audit logs can be exported to S3 in the same region. Default retention is 90 days on our side; on Private deployments we can configure longer retention or automatic export to the customer's S3 bucket for indefinite retention per contract. SIEM pull: we can provide a CloudWatch -> Kinesis/Firehose export pattern or direct S3 export for Veridian to ingest into their SIEM.

Attachments I'm preparing: network_diagram_veridian_vpc.pdf, kms_integration_summary.pdf, soc2_control_mapping.xlsx.

Limitations / notes:
- If Veridian requires the entire control plane to be customer-run (no Redwood-managed control plane components), timeline extends by 4-6 weeks for approval and installation.
- BYOK requires admin key policy updates on the customer's KMS side to allow Redwood service principal access. Laura, please confirm any contract wording for that.

I'll finalize the diagrams and PDFs and drop them into the thread.

—Rishi

Team — SOC 2 and SIG notes for Veridian:

- SOC 2: Our most recent SOC 2 Type II report covers infrastructure, change management, logical access, and system operations. We can provide a redacted SOC 2 report to Veridian under an NDA (standard practice). Relevant control IDs in our internal mapping: INF-3 (infrastructure isolation), CHG-1 (change control), LOG-2 (audit logging).

- SIG/CAIQ: For data residency questions the applicable sections are mostly around network controls and key management. We can supply a filled CAIQ subset that references our VPC/private deployment guide and KMS integration notes.

- Data residency statement (draft): "For Private deployments configured to run in a single customer-selected AWS region, customer data (customer-provided inputs, model context, and generated outputs) will be persisted and processed only within the selected AWS region. System metadata required for operational health may be stored in the same region; Redwood will not replicate customer data outside of that region unless the customer explicitly enables cross-region replication."

- Audit logs: we can confirm audit logs are retained for 90 days by default and can be exported to the customer's regional S3 bucket. We can also provide signed hash manifests of exported logs on request for audit purposes.

I'll attach a redacted SOC2 checklist and a CAIQ excerpt. Laura, any legal constraints on the draft language?

—Monica
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference

- SOC 2 / SIG: Redacted SOC 2 Type II report and CAIQ subset attached. The soc2_control_mapping.xlsx maps key controls relevant to Veridian's questions.
- Audit logs: Default retention 90 days; we can export logs to your regional S3 bucket for indefinite retention. We can provide an automated export pattern for SIEM ingestion.

Attachments provided: network_diagram_veridian_vpc.pdf, kms_integration_summary.pdf, soc2_control_mapping.xlsx.
